channel.title: Kronos Fusion Energy — News
channel.description: News and dated research results from Kronos Fusion Energy, a family-owned American fusion company — each item linked to its published record. Breeder and generator physics, in the open.

item.title: Checking Our Work: The Benchmark Harness and the Codes We Run Against
item.description: Kronos runs its own design choices through an independent turbulence code rather than grading them with its own toolkit alone, and says plainly where the two still disagree.

item.title: Design Locked: The Breeding Blanket
item.description: Kronos has locked the reference design for the shell that turns fusion neutrons into tritium fuel, fixing its zoning and material placement to a breeding ratio with margin to spare.

item.title: Kronos Weighs Isotope Yield Against the Breeder's Neutron Budget
item.description: Every neutron the breeder produces is already accounted for before any isotope beyond tritium, including helium-3, can draw against the same budget.

item.title: Gate closed: the breeder's magnet set fails safe on quench
item.description: Kronos has closed the base quench-protection gate behind the 16.84 T centrepost field, engineering a controlled shutdown into the coil set rather than leaving failure to chance.

item.title: Burner's Neutron Fraction Characterized at 5.44 Percent
item.description: A low-neutron result from the D-helium-3 burner is the physical basis for both of its fixed, non-naval housings.

item.title: Inside the Engine That Re-Derives Kronos's Headline Q = 3.076
item.description: The breeder's frozen fusion-gain figure is not a stored constant — it is recomputed from scratch every time Kronos's evaluator runs, and checked cold across independent environments before it is trusted.

item.title: Design locked: first-wall material selection
item.description: Kronos has locked the reference material and panel arrangement for the breeder's first wall, the component most directly exposed to the burning plasma of anything in the machine.

item.title: Kronos Publishes the Actual Code Behind Its Design-Point Numbers
item.description: The evaluator engine that re-derives the breeder's and burner's headline gain figures is public on GitHub, not a simplified stand-in.

item.title: Neutronics: What Becomes Radioactive, and for How Long
item.description: The same 14.1 MeV neutron flux that lets Hyperion breed tritium also activates the structure around it; Kronos is tracking that inventory as a distinct analysis from the breeding calculation itself.

item.title: Gate Closed: The Cryogenic Heat Load Balances at 20 K
item.description: Kronos has closed the de-risking gate confirming its magnet cooling system clears the heat load it will see, at a cold point far less demanding than traditional superconductor baths.

item.title: Kronos Ties Every Published Figure Back to Its Source Numbers
item.description: A canon-lock pipeline generates Kronos's charts directly from the same design-point data the papers cite, so a figure can never silently drift from the number behind it.

item.title: AI + Quantum method ships with a three-environment cold reproduction
item.description: Rather than asserting its method runs cleanly, Kronos ran it from scratch in three separate environments and published the log showing each one reached the same answer.

item.title: Kronos Maps What the Breeder's Center-Stack Shield Has to Stop
item.description: A neutronics analysis lays out the flux the Hyperion breeder's innermost shield has to absorb, ahead of the specific attenuation numbers.

item.title: Kronos Freezes Burner Engineering Gain at Q_E = 1.318
item.description: The honest efficiency figure for a burner whose real value is low-neutron output, not raw fusion power, is now locked at the frozen design point.

item.title: Burner Direct-Conversion Efficiency Frozen at η = 0.49
item.description: Kronos has frozen the direct energy-conversion efficiency for its D-³He burner line at 0.49, using a five-channel stack to capture charged-particle exhaust without ever routing it through a thermal cycle.

item.title: Design Locked: Hyperion's Divertor and Exhaust Path
item.description: The breeder's negative-triangularity shape steadies the plasma edge, letting Kronos lock a reference geometry for channeling exhaust heat away from the core.

item.title: De-Risking Register Evidence Base Posted as a Live Deposit
item.description: Kronos has put its gate-by-gate evidence methodology on the open record, so headline figures like Q = 3.076 and the passing centrepost stress trace back to a checkable entry rather than standing as bare assertions.

item.title: Neutronics: The Blanket's Breeding Margin, at the Frozen Point
item.description: Kronos has published the reaction accounting behind its headline breeding ratio, tracking every neutron born in the plasma to see how much of it becomes tritium fuel.

item.title: Kronos Closes De-Risking Gate on Fast-Acting Plasma Fault Control
item.description: A vertical-displacement event can end a discharge and load the vessel hard if it isn't caught early; Kronos says its control system catches one at the plasma's own timescale in simulation.

item.title: Gate closed: negative-triangularity shaping validated in nonlinear CGYRO
item.description: Simulation confirms the breeder's outward-pointing D-shape suppresses the edge turbulence behind one of a compact tokamak's sharpest failure modes.

item.title: Kronos Scopes What Its Simulation Stack Can Model Today
item.description: A layered approach to simulation keeps each code answering only the physics question it was built for, and says plainly which parts are still being integrated.

item.title: Kronos Locks the Breeder's Magnet-Set Geometry
item.description: The coil layout behind Hyperion's frozen field profile is now fixed, giving every downstream structural, quench, and thermal analysis a stable reference to check against.

item.title: CGYRO turbulence dataset now carries a permanent DOI
item.description: The nonlinear gyrokinetic simulation runs behind Kronos's negative-triangularity shaping choice are now posted as a versioned, citable dataset, open for independent comparison.

item.title: Structural Analysis Maps the Forces Hyperion's Own Field Creates
item.description: At a plasma current of 9.66 MA inside a 16.84-tesla field, the electromagnetic forces on the breeder's magnet set and vessel are a primary structural load, not an afterthought.

item.title: Breeder Plasma Current Frozen at 9.66 MA
item.description: Fixing Hyperion's plasma current to a single reference value lets structural, shielding, and control teams design against one number instead of a range.

item.title: A Digital Twin of the Breeder, Component by Component
item.description: Kronos has published a clickable, component-level model of the Hyperion breeder, built directly on the frozen design point, so the machine can be inspected years before any steel is cut.

item.title: Kronos Locks the Design of the Breeder's Vacuum Vessel Shell
item.description: The structural boundary that holds plasma vacuum against atmosphere is now fixed to a reference geometry, giving every downstream structural check a stable target.

item.title: Gate closed: fluence budget sets the breeder centrepost's replacement life
item.description: Kronos has turned years of neutron damage into a defined service-life number for the column carrying the breeder's 16.84 T core field, rather than leaving the question open-ended.

item.title: Breeder's Fusion-Power Point Frozen at 85.04 Megawatts
item.description: Every downstream engineering budget on the Hyperion breeder now scales from a single frozen power figure, anchored to materials output rather than electricity.

item.title: Kronos Publishes REBCO Tape Qualification Data as a Standalone Descriptor
item.description: A precise, reusable record of how the superconducting tape behind both machines' magnets was qualified is now public in its own right, separate from the paper that argues the physics.

item.title: REBCO magnet and tape basis released as a citable dataset
item.description: Kronos has posted the REBCO superconductor basis behind its highest-field magnet as an open, citable dataset — the reference every downstream magnet and thermal analysis in the breeder program cites back to.

item.title: Structural Analysis Traces Gravity Loads From Magnets to Foundation
item.description: A new load-path study checks that Hyperion's heaviest components, anchored by the 16.84-tesla centrepost magnet set, can be supported without misaligning the machine's field.

item.title: Gate Closed: Center-Stack Shielding Protects the Core Column
item.description: Kronos has locked the shield's layer count and material sequencing around the centrepost, closing a de-risking gate long before the column carrying 16.84 T ever sees a real neutron.

item.title: Breeder Fusion Gain Frozen at Q = 3.076
item.description: Kronos has frozen the fusion-gain figure the rest of the breeder platform is designed against, and judges Hyperion on the materials it produces rather than on electricity.

item.title: Kronos Publishes the REBCO Conductor Basis Behind Both Machines
item.description: A new open dataset documents the high-temperature superconducting tape that makes both the breeder's centrepost field and the burner's plug field possible in a compact envelope.

item.title: Recompute it yourself: Kronos puts its validators live in the browser
item.description: Every claim in Kronos's de-risking register, from tritium breeding to magnet field strength, can now be recalculated live in the browser instead of taken on faith from a static number.

item.title: Design Locked: Center-Stack Shielding for the Breeder's Core
item.description: The shield around the machine's most exposed structural column now has a fixed reference layout, ahead of the detailed engineering paper.

item.title: Kronos Posts Burner Design-Point Dataset for Independent Reproduction
item.description: Every input behind the burner's headline efficiency and gain figures is now downloadable, so an outside reader can re-derive the numbers rather than take them on trust.

item.title: Structural: the vacuum vessel's 1-D thermal profile
item.description: A new thermal analysis maps the temperature gradient across the vacuum vessel wall, the input every downstream stress calculation for the vessel — including the centrepost's own structural result — depends on.

item.title: Gate Closed: Hyperion's Centrepost Passes Its Structural Margin at 181 MPa
item.description: The column carrying the breeder's 16.84-tesla core field has cleared its de-risking check, the load-bearing result every downstream shielding and thermal analysis is measured against.

item.title: Centrepost Stress Passes With Margin at 181 MPa
item.description: A finite-element check of Hyperion's most heavily loaded structural column clears its material limit at the frozen design point, freeing the rest of the radial build to proceed on fixed numbers.

item.title: Burner Design Point Published: The D–³He Tandem-Mirror Reference Case
item.description: Kronos has fixed the numbers behind its low-neutron burner line, the shared physics core that both the Aegis defense generator and the MetroVolt data-center generator build outward from.

item.title: Kronos Opens the Physics Engine Behind Its Published Numbers
item.description: Kronos has released the toolkit it uses internally to derive its frozen design points, putting the evaluator behind the breeder and burner numbers into anyone's hands.

item.title: Design locked: breeder's cryogenic network fixed at 20 K
item.description: Kronos has frozen the closed-cycle cooling architecture behind its breeder's magnets, the choice that lets a 16.84 T centrepost fit inside a compact machine instead of a much larger one.

item.title: Kronos Posts Breeder Design-Point Dataset to Zenodo
item.description: The frozen numbers behind the Hyperion breeder are now a permanent, versioned Zenodo record instead of figures quoted only in a paper.

item.title: Kronos Publishes Full Turbulence Run Behind Breeder's Negative-Triangularity Shaping
item.description: A nonlinear gyrokinetic simulation, not a linear estimate, now backs the plasma-shaping choice meant to steady the breeder's edge without leaning on a disruption-prone confinement barrier.

item.title: Gate closed: net tritium breeding clears self-sufficiency
item.description: Kronos has closed the de-risking gate confirming the Hyperion breeder's blanket produces more tritium than it burns, with margin to spare for decay losses and startup fuel for the next machine.

item.title: Breeder Design Confirms Net Tritium Self-Sufficiency at TBR ≥ 1.05
item.description: Modeled neutronics across Hyperion's blanket show the breeder produces more tritium than it burns, with margin held in reserve for decay and future startup fuel.

item.title: Breeder Design Point Published: Hyperion's Q = 3.076 Reference Case
item.description: Kronos has frozen the numbers behind its Hyperion breeder, giving every downstream design paper in the series a single, fixed target to match.

item.title: The Horizon: Toward Gate-Stage Hardware
item.description: As 2026 closes, Kronos looks ahead to its gated program — engaging vendors and the supply chain on the path from a validated design toward first hardware.

item.title: Load-Following Capability Modeled for Grid Integration
item.description: Kronos models load-following capability for grid integration in its design point, ahead of the gated program.

item.title: Microsecond AI Control Modeled for Vertical Displacement Events
item.description: Simulations show the microsecond AI digital twin can mitigate vertical displacement events (VDEs) in the design.

item.title: Center-Stack Neutron Shield and Fluence Budget Analyzed
item.description: 2026 simulation campaigns analyze the shielded center-stack neutron-fluence budget for the low-neutron design — no breeding blanket required.

item.title: The 20 K Closed-Cycle Cryogenic Network Design Locked
item.description: Kronos locks the design of its 20 K closed-cycle cryogenic network, eliminating liquid-helium infrastructure from the balance-of-plant.

item.title: 1-D Thermal Gradient and Vacuum Vessel Structural Analysis Published
item.description: Kronos publishes its 1-D thermal-gradient (1700 C plasma edge) data and full vacuum-vessel structural analysis.

item.title: The 2026 Tech Audit Presentation Delivered
item.description: Kronos delivers its 2026 Tech Audit - a full disclosure of generator physics and engineering.

item.title: Entering the Pre-Commercial Validation Stage
item.description: Kronos transitions out of conceptual R&D into the pre-commercial validation stage for the S.M.A.R.T. generator family.

item.title: The Autonomous AI Stability System Detailed
item.description: Kronos details the design of its autonomous AI stability ('immune') system for real-time plasma control.

item.title: The Staged Fuel Cycle Strategy Solidified
item.description: Kronos solidifies its staged fuel-cycle strategy, bridging near-term commissioning toward low-neutron D-3He operation.

item.title: Expansion of the Simulation Suite to 12 Modules
item.description: The Kronos AI simulation suite expands to twelve interoperable modules spanning magnets, plasma, and balance-of-plant.

item.title: Channel 3 & 4: Thermionic and Photovoltaic Energy Capture
item.description: DEC Channels 3 and 4 - thermionic emission and photovoltaic capture - finalize designs to harvest surface heat and radiation.

item.title: Channel 1 & 2: Electrostatic and MHD Extraction Maturation
item.description: DEC Channels 1 and 2 - electrostatic retarding-field and MHD extraction - mature through 2025 engineering.

item.title: The 5-Channel Direct Energy Conversion (DEC) Blueprint
item.description: Kronos publishes the complete engineering blueprint for its 5-channel Direct Energy Conversion system.

item.title: The AEGIS System for Modular Defense Applications
item.description: Kronos unveils AEGIS, a hardened, modular generator line for defense, remote, and critical-infrastructure missions.

item.title: Formal Introduction of the MetroVolt Urban Generator
item.description: Kronos formally introduces MetroVolt, its commercial urban fusion generator.

item.title: Priyanca Ford's Q1 Founder Update
item.description: Founder Priyanca Ford's Q1 update on the company's long-run ambitions and program direction.

item.title: Simulation Validates Negative Triangularity Plasma Shaping
item.description: Kronos's simulation suite validates negative-triangularity plasma shaping for the S.M.A.R.T. reactor - suppressing edge instabilities without H-mode.

item.title: Jack Dongarra Optimizes Exascale Computing Workflows
item.description: Turing Award winner Jack Dongarra advises on optimizing the exascale computing workflows behind the digital twin.

item.title: Sushma Bhatia Steers Legislative and Environmental Strategy
item.description: Advisory board member Sushma Bhatia steers the company's legislative and environmental strategy.

item.title: Ruben Fair's Expertise Applied to Magnetic Shielding
item.description: Board advisor Ruben Fair brings three decades of magnet-design and magnetic-shielding expertise to the program.

item.title: Dr. Gerald Kulcinski Champions the Aneutronic Vision
item.description: Fusion pioneer Dr. Gerald Kulcinski joins the podcast, validating the low-neutron D-3He pathway and its aneutronic p-11B endpoint.

item.title: "The Kronos Fusion Energy Podcast" Expands Educational Reach
item.description: 'The Kronos Fusion Energy Podcast,' hosted by Priyanca Ford, expands to demystify fusion and engage tier-one talent.

item.title: Synergies with MagLab Enhance High-Temperature Superconductors
item.description: Work at the National High Magnetic Field Laboratory advances characterization of the high-temperature superconducting (REBCO) tapes central to the magnet system.

item.title: World's First Component Factory Established in India
item.description: Kronos establishes its first Fusion Energy Component Factory in India, executing on international scaling.

item.title: Jon Michel Greenwood Spearheads Digital Twin Architecture
item.description: CTO Jon Michel Greenwood elevates the Kronos simulation suite into a fully realized digital-twin platform.

item.title: Global Call for Supply Chain Partnerships
item.description: Kronos launches a Supply Chain Partnership Portal, marking the transition from design toward manufacturing readiness.

item.title: Establishing the KFEDS Defense Security Posture
item.description: Kronos formalizes the KFEDS defense security posture, highlighting the resilience advantages of compact fusion for critical infrastructure.

item.title: PUZZLE X 2023: The Helium-3 Dawn Presented
item.description: Founder Priyanca Ford delivers the keynote 'From Star Power to Earth: Helium-3 & the Dawn of the Fusion Era' at PUZZLE X in Barcelona.

item.title: Alignment with the DOE Milestone-Based Fusion Program
item.description: Kronos aligns its development plan with the U.S. Department of Energy's Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program.

item.title: Global Community Invited to Beta Test Algorithms
item.description: In an unusual move for a private fusion developer, Kronos opens its simulation suite to a global community of beta testers.

item.title: Unveiling of the AI/ML-Powered Simulation Suite
item.description: Kronos unveils its AI/ML-powered simulation suite - the computational backbone that would grow into the company's digital twin.

item.title: Paul Weiss Elevated to Lead Material Sciences & Nano Technology
item.description: Dr. Paul Weiss, holder of the Fred Kavli Chair in NanoSystems Sciences, formally takes the helm of Material Sciences & Nano Technology.

item.title: Staged Fuel-Cycle Strategy Initiated
item.description: Kronos launches its staged fuel-cycle strategy — bridging a brief deuterium–tritium commissioning stage toward low-neutron deuterium–helium-3 operation, with helium-3 bred in situ via catalyzed D–D (no breeding blanket).
